result.summary: Adds sync and lookup microbenchmarks for TxIndex, TxoSpenderIndex, and BlockFilterIndex, backed by shared test utilities that generate synthetic blocks with chained spends and distinct output scripts. Also adds documentation in doc/benchmarking.md explaining how to profile benchmark I/O syscalls, peak resident memory, and disk usage.
result.problem: Evaluating performance changes to the index subsystem previously required running a full initial block download. The only existing index benchmark, BlockFilterIndexSync, only processed coinbase-only blocks, leaving no benchmarks for TxIndex or TxoSpenderIndex and no way to measure index behavior against transaction counts or distinct script outputs.
evidence: Author notes in PR description: 'There is a fair amount of work going into the indices at the moment, and no cheap way to tell whether a change actually improves what it set out to improve: checking end to end means a full IBD. The only index benchmark in the tree, BlockFilterIndexSync, syncs coinbase-only blocks, so it cannot show anything that scales with what a block contains, and there is none at all for TxIndex or TxoSpenderIndex.'

Author demonstrated utility in existing PRs: '#35531 (5-byte siphash keys) trades a 49% smaller index on disk for a lookup regression that grows with index size, and #34489 (batch db writes) cuts write syscalls by 91% with CPU unchanged.'
result.scope_notes: Touches only benchmark harness code and developer documentation.
result.changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the benchmark code or documentation; only minor commit metadata or rebase adjustments.
result.card: Adds sync and lookup benchmarks for TxIndex, TxoSpenderIndex, and realistic BlockFilterIndex workloads, alongside documentation on measuring benchmark I/O and peak memory. Evaluating index changes previously required a full initial block download, as the only existing benchmark processed coinbase-only blocks and could not test transaction-level indexing. The author used these benchmarks on PR 35531 and PR 34489 to measure index disk reduction, lookup regressions, and a 91 percent drop in write syscalls.

risk.why: Only touches benchmark targets and documentation without altering production node logic.
